title: AI Art Styles
summary: See 18 AI art styles side by side, from watercolor and ukiyo-e to pixel art and film noir, with the words that call up each look and a way to try them free.
body_markdown:
### What are the most popular AI art styles?


Photorealism, anime, watercolor, oil painting, pixel art, comic book and 3D render appear on most lists of AI art styles. Which works best depends on what you are making and who it is for.


### How do I get a specific art style in AI?


Name the medium, the line and the palette in your prompt, such as two-color linocut or loose watercolor with thin ink outlines. Attaching a reference image in that style makes the result much more consistent.


### How many art styles are there?


There is no fixed number, since every movement, medium and artist can become a style. Flickpedia holds hundreds of visual styles grouped into cinematic, illustration, painting, drawing, 3D, anime and cartoon.


### Can I keep one art style across many images?


Yes. Reuse the same style line and the same reference image in every prompt, and check each new image against the first one, so a series or a whole film stays in one look.


### What is the difference between an art style and a filter?


A filter changes a finished image, while an art style shapes how the image is made, from its lines to its light. Asking for a style in the prompt gives a result that looks drawn or painted rather than processed.


### Can AI art styles be used in video?


Yes. In Flick you can make a first image in a style and animate it, which keeps the look in motion for a short film, an ad or a music video.
